_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Cron-job architecture for web applications — Inngest schedule integration, Vercel Cron configuration, retry logic,…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "design a daily cron that triggers a report job without timing out"
cases.context: The agent has access to the cron-scheduling skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is cron-scheduling the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes cron-scheduling as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against background-jobs, real-time-updates, observability-modeling
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the cron-scheduling workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore cron-scheduling
Does not route to background-jobs, real-time-updates, observability-modeling when the cron-scheduling scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence
